findings.headline: 99215 at 14.5% vs 3.6% expected; 6 of 29 random charts support a lower level, including 4 of 6 99215s
findings.interpretation: Large practice (2,390 claims). 80% of its 99215s are on patients with 0 or 1 chronic conditions, and the 99215 share is high even with 0 conditions (12% vs 4%). The chart rule triggered: 6 of 29 random charts are documented below the billed level, and 4 of the 6 sampled 99215s were documented as moderate MDM (comparison providers 39%). 48% of notes address fewer problems than the billed level implies. No data-quality flags. The overpayment estimate is not reliable (only 6 charts in the 99215 stratum), so no dollar figure is quoted. Next step: a certified coder re-scores the records.

findings.headline: 22% 99215 vs 5% expected, mostly on low-complexity patients; notes look written up to match the bill
findings.interpretation: 56% of its 99215s are on patients with 0 or 1 conditions. The chart rule did not trigger (0 of 9 99215s scored below billed). The summary rule flags the notes as inflated: 47% address fewer problems than the claimed level implies, 17% signed late, 17% duplicated, and the audit trail shows 13% bulk-created and 13% paste-heavy notes. Honest practices show some of these signs too. This finding rests on note-versus-claim signals, not on re-scoring, so a coder should confirm it before any recovery. No data-quality flags.

findings.headline: Highest screen score (37% 99215), but charts and audit trail support the billing
